findings: The repository source identifies LeetCode 1769, and the official problem defines a binary boxes string, unit adjacent moves, and an independently calculated minimum operation count for every target box.
The candidate derives the exact distance-sum objective and explains the left/right incremental recurrence instead of presenting the O(n) code as an unexplained trick.
The update order is explained correctly: current side cost is consumed before the current-position ball contributes one extra move to the next target.

An independent direct-distance oracle validates all binary strings through length 10 plus maximum-length structured cases; this is distinct from the writer harness and reaches the official n=2000 boundary.
The stated int bound is conservative and validated: with n=2000 and all boxes occupied, the maximum endpoint cost is 1,999,000.
The answer includes problem-specific follow-ups, failure boundaries, complexity, and does not fabricate production experience.
